title: AI Infrastructure: From Federal Priority To Assured Operation
summary: Follow federal AI and R&D direction through compute, power, chips, procurement, critical-infrastructure assurance, implementation, and measured operating evidence.
current_state_summary: Federal records now make the infrastructure and assurance stack explicit, but policy direction, purchasing channels, and profile development remain upstream of validated institutional deployment.
current_state: FY2027 federal R&D guidance connects AI and quantum priorities to chips, power, manufacturing, materials, and workforce.
The national-security policy stack adds secure compute, supply-chain resilience, acquisition, cybersecurity, and assurance requirements.
NIST has opened a critical-infrastructure AI RMF profile process that names deterministic behavior, explainability, graceful degradation, fail-safe operation, TEVV, and supply-chain visibility.
OMB and GSA records define use, acquisition, and purchasing rails without proving agency orders, integration, authorization, performance, or outcomes.
The pathway still lacks institution-level inventories, adopted profiles, validated controls, operating evidence, incident results, and measured mission value.

dependency_stack.current_state: Policy and R&D records identify AI, compute, chips, power, security, manufacturing, and talent as a connected national stack.
dependency_stack.boundary: Priority language does not establish appropriations, agency programs, infrastructure delivery, or technical outcomes.

dependency_stack.current_state: OMB, GSA, and prototype-agreement records expose governance, purchasing, contract-value, and initial-obligation rails.
dependency_stack.boundary: A purchasing channel, ceiling value, or initial obligation does not prove an order, deployment, authorization, usage, or mission outcome.

dependency_stack.current_state: NIST's concept identifies a sector profile and specific assurance properties for AI in IT, OT, and industrial control systems.
dependency_stack.boundary: The concept is not a draft profile, final guidance, mandate, validated test method, adopted control set, or deployed system.

dependency_stack.current_state: No current pathway record closes the loop from policy and acquisition into independently validated operating performance.
dependency_stack.boundary: Operating claims require named systems, inventories, controls, authorization, tests, incidents, maintenance, and measured outcomes.

evidence_limits: The pathway connects policy and infrastructure dependencies without claiming that federal agencies have completed implementation.
National-security and critical-infrastructure direction does not prove available high-security compute, resilient supply chains, or effective assurance.
Prototype agreements and buying channels are not equivalent to delivered, authorized, adopted, or successful systems.
next_records: Agency AI inventories, implementation plans, orders, contract clauses, authorizations, evaluations, incident records, renewals, and measured outcomes.
NIST critical-infrastructure profile drafts, public comments, final guidance, TEVV methods, sector adoption, procurement language, and operator evidence.
Facility-level compute, power, cooling, supply-chain, cybersecurity, and workforce records tied to named deployments.
